result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.modularity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Score a partition of the nodes into communities by its modularity. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L29957-L30053){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.modularity( communities, resolution=1.0, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Modularity](/assets/graphs/modularity.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The two-cluster graph with 9 edges, split into the partition you pass: A, B, C (teal) and D, E, F, G (violet). The card scores each community as its share of edges inside minus the share expected by chance, 3/9 − (7/18)² and 5/9 − (11/18)², each 0.18, for a modularity Q of 0.36." width="100%"} Modularity compares the fraction of edges that fall inside communities with the fraction expected if edges were placed at random while keeping every node's degree. A partition into dense, sparsely interconnected groups scores well above `0` (values of `0.3` to `0.7` are typical of clear community structure); putting all nodes in one community scores exactly `0`, and partitions that cut through dense regions score below `0`. For an undirected graph with `m` edges this is the Newman-Girvan modularity, `Q = Σ_c [ L_c / m - γ (D_c / 2m)² ]` where `L_c` is the number of edges inside community `c` and `D_c` is the sum of its nodes' degrees. Directed graphs use the Leicht-Newman version, which compares edges against out-degree × in-degree. On a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`) edge weights replace edge counts. The results match NetworkX's `community.modularity()`. Use this to compare the output of different community detection methods, to pick a `resolution=`, or to evaluate a partition you already have, such as known labels. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [communities]{.doc-parameter-name} : The partition to score, as any of: (1) the name of a node attribute holding community labels (e.g. `"cmty_louvain"` after `cmty_louvain()`), (2) a dictionary mapping node IDs or labels to community labels, as returned by the `cmty_*` methods with `return_dict=True`, or (3) a list of node groups, each a list or set of node IDs or labels. Every node must belong to exactly one community. [resolution]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The resolution parameter `γ`. Values above `1` reward smaller communities and values below `1` larger ones. Default is `1.0`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The modularity of the partition. A graph without edges scores `0`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node is missing from the partition, appears in two groups, or a label or attribute does not exist. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles joined by a bridge: splitting them apart scores well, while keeping all nodes together scores `0` and a split that cuts the triangles scores below `0`: ::: {#b5c596e6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) ( round(graph.modularity([["A", "B", "C"], ["D", "E", "F"]]), 3), graph.modularity([["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]]), round(graph.modularity([["A", "D"], ["B", "E"], ["C", "F"]]), 3), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (0.357, 0.0, -0.337) ``` ::: ::: Community detection results can be scored directly, from the stored attribute or the returned dictionary: ::: {#06b15c58 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.cmty_leiden(seed=1) graph.modularity("cmty_leiden"), graph.modularity(graph.cmty_louvain(return_dict=True)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (0.3571428571428571, 0.3571428571428571) ``` ::: :::
